title: Principal refinements and local algebra of Noetherian formal affine charts
statement: A locally Noetherian adic formal scheme $\mathfrak T$ is a ringed space covered by $\operatorname{Spf}R$, for commutative Noetherian rings $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal $K$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; the points of $\operatorname{Spf}R$ are the primes containing $K$, with the subspace topology from $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and its structure sheaf is the inverse limit of those of $\operatorname{Spec}(R/K^n)$. For $s\in R$ write $R_{\{s\}}=\varprojlim_n(R/K^n)_s$, equivalently the $KR_s$-adic completion of the ring localization $R_s$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The principal open $D(s)\cap\operatorname{Spf}R$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spf}R_{\{s\}}$; its ring $R_{\{s\}}$ is Noetherian, and restriction of sections is the canonical map $R\to R_s\to R_{\{s\}}$. These identifications commute with restrictions and continuous ring maps. For any two formal affine opens $U,V\subseteq\mathfrak T$, any point $x\in U\cap V$ and any open neighbourhood $N\subseteq U\cap V$ of $x$, there is a neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of $x$ that is principal in both $U$ and $V$. Finally, every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$ contains $K$. If $s\notin\mathfrak m$, there is an open maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\subset R_{\{s\}}$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$, and the induced map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to(R_{\{s\}})_{\mathfrak n}$ is faithfully flat: flat with surjective map on prime spectra [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. No quasi-excellence or regularity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use positive indices $n\geq1$. By the definition of a locally Noetherian adic formal scheme, work on a chart with $R\cong\varprojlim_nR/K^n$. An open prime contains some $K^n$, hence contains $K$, and conversely a prime containing $K$ is open. Thus the underlying space is $V(K)$, with its subspace topology, also the underlying space of every $\operatorname{Spec}(R/K^n)$. A principal open of this space is $D(s)\cap V(K)$; these form a basis because a Zariski open is a union of complements of vanishing sets of single elements. Regard the quotient structure sheaves as sheaves on this common space and use their inverse limit as the structure sheaf, exactly as in the formal-spectrum construction in Tag 0AHY. All operations are componentwise; the topologies on sections are the inverse-limit topologies of the discrete quotient section rings.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, definition of Spf and its structure sheaf

proof.text: The inverse system here is indexed by the small category of positive integers, with arrows from larger indices to smaller ones. Apply sectionwise limits of sheaves of sets to its underlying sheaves. Componentwise addition and multiplication make this the limit ring sheaf as well. On $D(s)\cap V(K)$ the affine scheme section formula at level $n$ gives $(R/K^n)_s$. Consequently its section ring is $C_s:=\varprojlim_n(R/K^n)_s$. The restriction from the whole chart sends $r$ to $(r\bmod K^n)_n$ followed by localization at each level; it is the canonical composite $R\to R_s\to C_s$. Restrictions between smaller basis opens are likewise the compatible quotient-localization maps, rather than arbitrarily chosen ring isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, displayed formula for sections on D(f); Tags 00W2 (sites.tex lemma-limit-sheaf) and 01HV/01I3 (schemes.tex lemma-spec-sheaves/lemma-standard-open-affine)

proof.text: Localization commutes with quotient, so $R_s/(KR_s)^n\cong(R/K^n)_s$, with $r/s^e$ mapping to $(r\bmod K^n)/s^e$. This identifies $C_s$ with the $KR_s$-adic completion of $R_s$. The ideal $KR_s$ is finitely generated by the images of any finite generating set of $K$. The completion-quotient theorem, applied with module $M=R_s$, gives $C_s/(KC_s)^n\cong(R/K^n)_s$ with the displayed projections, and completeness and separatedness of $C_s$. Localization preserves Noetherianity and Noetherian completion preserves it, so $C_s$ is Noetherian. The special-fibre isomorphism identifies $V(KC_s)$ with $D(s)\cap V(K)$. These identifications identify all thickening structure sheaves: on the basis given by the images of $a\in R$, the level-$n$ section map is precisely $((R/K^n)_s)_a\cong(R/K^n)_{sa}$. This basis suffices since every element of $C_s/KC_s=(R/K)_s$ is $\bar a/\bar s^e$. Taking the componentwise limits from Step 2 identifies the sheaves, including their topologies, and proves $D(s)\cap\operatorname{Spf}R\cong\operatorname{Spf}C_s$.

For a continuous ring map $\varphi:(R,K)\to(S,L)$, for each $n$ choose $m(n)$ with $\varphi(K^{m(n)})\subseteq L^n$. Enlarge the choices to make them nondecreasing. The induced maps $R/K^{m(n)}\to S/L^n$ induce $(R/K^{m(n)})_s\to(S/L^n)_{\varphi(s)}$, sending $\bar r/\bar s^e$ to $\overline{\varphi(r)}/\overline{\varphi(s)}^e$. For a compatible tuple, use its $m(n)$ component to define the $n$ component of the image. The quotient transition maps make these images compatible. Two choices agree after passing to the larger index, so the map is independent of the choices. Restriction squares commute since both paths have the displayed fraction formula at each quotient. Composites of continuous maps give the composite fraction formula after enlarging indices; identities do also. Thus the principal-chart identifications and the restriction maps commute with continuous ring maps, including maps which do not carry $K$ itself into $L$.

source.place: Tags 0AHY and 0AHZ (equation-morphisms-affine-formal-schemes); construction on quotients, with reindexing for continuity

proof.text: On any of these charts, $D(s)$ is intrinsically the locus where the germ of $s$ is invertible: on $D(s)$ the inverses in all quotient localizations give an inverse section by Step 2. Conversely, the projection to the first quotient sheaf and then to the residue field at a prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq K$ sends an invertible germ to a nonzero element, forcing $s\notin\mathfrak p$. This characterization is unchanged under restriction to an open ringed subspace, since its germs are the same. Thus the principal loci computed in two overlapping charts agree whenever their sections agree after restriction.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, quotient-sheaf construction and principal sections; explicit germ argument

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spf}R$, $V=\operatorname{Spf}S$. Choose $f\in R$ with $x\in U'=D_U(f)\subseteq N$, using the basis in Step 1. By Step 3, $U'=\operatorname{Spf}C_f$ with section ring $C_f$. Choose $g\in S$ with $x\in W=D_V(g)\subseteq U'$. Let $t$ be the restriction of $g$ to $U'$. By Step 5 its invertibility locus on $U'$ is exactly $W$. The quotient formula of Step 3 writes $t\bmod KC_f=\bar a/\bar f^e$ for some $a\in R$. For the primes of $C_f$ containing $KC_f$, nonvanishing of $t$ is therefore nonvanishing of $a$, since $f$ is invertible. Hence $W=D_U(fa)$ as a subset of $U$, while $W=D_V(g)$ by construction. These are open ringed subspaces with the inherited structure sheaf. Thus $W$ contains $x$, lies in $N$, and is principal in both original charts. Notice that only the reduction of $t$ is written as a fraction; $t$ itself need not belong to the ordinary localization $R_f$.

source.place: Tag 01IW, lemma-standard-open-two-affines, adapted using the completed-localization reduction of algebra.tex Tag 05GG; explicit argument

proof.text: Apply the complete-ring Jacobson-radical lemma to $(R,K)$. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$ therefore contains $K$. If $s\notin\mathfrak m$, the first-quotient projection gives the surjection $C_s\to(R/K)_s\to R/\mathfrak m$, the second arrow being $\bar a/\bar s^e\mapsto(a\bmod\mathfrak m)(s\bmod\mathfrak m)^{-e}$. This composite is surjective since its restriction to $R$ is the residue map. Its kernel $\mathfrak n$ is maximal (its quotient is the field $R/\mathfrak m$), contains $KC_s$, and contracts to $\mathfrak m$. In particular it is an open maximal ideal of $C_s$.

The ring $R_s$ is Noetherian by Step 3. The map $R\to R_s$ is flat by flatness of localization, and $R_s\to C_s$ is flat by flatness of Noetherian adic completion, applied to $KR_s$. Composition of flat ring maps gives flatness of $R\to C_s$. Apply flat localization of a ring map at $\mathfrak n$, whose preimage is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ by Step 7, to obtain a flat local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak m}\to(C_s)_{\mathfrak n}$. The flat-local faithful-flatness lemma makes it faithfully flat and gives surjectivity on prime spectra. This proves the last assertion using just Noetherianity and the adic hypotheses; no regularity or quasi-excellence was used.
